13 Peaks Challenge

By: Laura Byrne | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
One little girl on a big mission: climbing the Western Cape's most challenging peaks in an effort to support rhino orphans.

Unique Selling Point:
Mackenzie Knott is just 11 years old, but she has just completed her fourth 13 Peaks Challenge. It's a journey of 110km with over 7000 metres of climbing, and it was designed by extreme endurance runner Ryan Sandes to link his favourite peaks of the Cape Peninsula into one "great adventure". Mackenzie has completed the 13 Peaks challenge every year for the past four years, starting when she was just 8 years old. She does it to raise money for rhino orphans, paying for up to 20 litres of milk that a single baby rhino can guzzle in a day.

Summary:
Kenzie is the mascot for Fit 4 Rhinos, a non-profit that seeks to tap into the relatively unexploited fitness community to raise moneys to support rhino orphans. Liezl Schoeman, the founder of Fit 4 Rhinos, met Kenzie's dad Gareth through their shared love of running, and soon became acquainted with Kenzie: a determined little girl intent on doing her bit to save the rhino from extinction. Gareth plans each challenge with Kenzie and runs alongside her as they tackle one of the 13 Peaks at a time.

Press Release:


The 13 Peaks Challenge is a journey of over 100 kilometres, climbing more than 6000 metres and conquering some of the Western Cape's most difficult mountain peaks. It was designed by an experienced extreme endurance runner, and it’s a tough adventure for even experienced adult trail runners. But that hasn’t deterred Mackenzie Knott, a sporty eleven-year-old with a passion for animals and the outdoors. Determined to raise funds for the care of rhino orphans, Mackenzie has taken on the gruelling 13 Peaks Challenge every year since she was just eight years old.

Script:


UPSOUND: GARETH KNOTT INSTAGRAM: Gareth: So where are we heading to now?
Kenzie: [inaudible]
Gareth: Grootkop! And where’s Grootkop? Up there.
LINK: It’s called the 13 Peaks Challenge, and it links up some of the Western Cape’s most daunting summits. Created by ultra-endurance runner Ryan Sandes, it covers some 100km and climbs more than 6000m.
UPSOUND: INSTAGRAM: We just did some intense - like, intense intense - climbing
VOICEOVER: It’s an attractive challenge for runners… and one of its fans is very diminutive indeed.
UPSOUND: INSTAGRAM: We have reached the summit of Suther Peak.
UPSOUND: YOUTUBE: Here we go!
VOCIEOVER: Gareth Knott took on the 13 Peaks in 2020.
UPSOUND: YOUTUBE: How does it feel?
Gareth: Beautiful. Beautiful pain.
VOICEOVER: He didn’t anticipate that his eight year-old daughter, Mackenzie, would be inspired to take on the challenge herself.
UPSOUND: MACKENZIE KNOTT: I saw my dad’s videos. And then I was like, I want to beat my dad!
UPSOUND: GARETH KNOTT: So we “started” the challenge, but I didn't think that she would summit Lion's Head at eight. But Kenzie was just like, alright, what's next? And so that's when it got real.
VOICEOVER: One outing at a time, Mackenzie went on to pull off the rest of the multi-day challenge.
UPSOUND: ERIN BATES: Did you know what you were getting yourself into?
MACKENZIE KNOTT: No. I was like, didn't know how far it was or anything. Even when I finished, I didn't know it was over 100km.
VOICEOVER: But the mountain bug had bitten. Mackenzie decided to take on the challenge again - with a purpose.
UPSOUND: INSTAGRAM: I’m looking forward to my 13 Peaks adventure for the baby rhinos.
UPSOUND: LIEZL SCHOEMAN: Actually, the only thing I could think of was, please just don't let this child fall off the mountain. But that was only a worry for the first day. And I was just like, you know what? This girl is a born trail runner.
VOICEOVER: Triathlete Liezl Schoeman founded the Fit 4 Rhinos initiative.
UPSOUND: LIEZL SCHOEMAN: Rhinos are called a keystone species, which means they are imperative to secure a healthy biodiversity level within the ecosystem. We actually host 80% of the rhino population worldwide, which has a massive impact for us in terms of tourism revenue.
LINK: In 2022, Mackenzie became a Fit 4 Rhinos ambassador, raising funds towards milk for orphan rhinos.
UPSOUND: LIEZL SCHOEMAN: The average baby rhino can consume between roughly 12l to about 21l of milk per day. So, for example, the price of three cappuccinos can buy a baby's breakfast, which is one six pack of fat free milk.
VOICEOVER: It’s become an annual fundraiser, bringing in nearly R26 000 to date.
UPSOUND: MACKENZIE KNOTT: I think I saved like six baby rhinos or something. Yeah, and I even got to name one.
ERIN BATES: That's so cool. What did you name it?
MACKENZIE KNOTT: Hazel June.
ERIN BATES: Wow.
MACKENZIE KNOTT: Yeah, I named it Hazel because I love that name, and June because I did 13 peaks in June.
UPSOUND: INSTAGRAM: So we are on our way to Muizenberg Peak. It’s a fresh breezy morning. And Aurora of course is being her own crazy self.
VOICEOVER: This month, Mackenzie took on the 13 Peaks for the fourth time.
UPSOUND: ERIN BATES: Do you think it's getting easier for you as you get older?
MACKENZIE KNOTT: Yeah. Because now I know the trails better. And I know how much distance I'm doing.
UPSOUND: INSTAGRAM: [Gareth] Tough start to the day, no switch backs on Klein Leeuwkop, everything just goes vertical.
UPSOUND: GARETH KNOTT: So we do a lot of prep before.
ERIN BATES: You're obviously like, coach. Cheerleader. Snack packer…
GARETH KNOTT: Navigator...um, I'm her pack. Uh, Packer. Uh, what's what do you call them?
ERIN BATES: Sherpa.
GARETH KNOTT: Sherpa [laughs] Um, I carry the food. I carry the clothing. Um. And then I have to constantly remind her about safety on the mountain. That's the most important thing.
UPSOUND: INSTAGRAM: It’s a very moody Table Mountain today - there’s no view.
UPSOUND: GARETH KNOTT: Sometimes it gets a little bit tricky with weather. [...] We've just sometimes got to be patient and take our time.
UPSOUN: INSTAGRAM: It was raining this morning and I was soaked, and now it’s sunny and it feels so good to have the sun on my face.
UPSOUND: LIEZL SCHOEMAN: From a confidence perspective, how she's grown within the last year is amazing. She also smacked PBs or personal bests on almost every peak.
UPSOUND: MACKENZIE KNOTT: It's very beautiful and peaceful in the mountains. And I like the birds, like the sounds of them, and it's just nice.
ERIN BATES: How many times are you planning on doing the 13 Peaks Challenge?
MACKENZIE KNOTT: Probably like for the rest of my life. [giggle]
UPSOUND: INSTAGRAM: Cocoa to the rescue!
